title: Declared repository structural placement
statement: Observed governed paths MUST conform to the repository structure declared by the project: implementation paths MUST occupy allowed top-level and owned roots, prohibited generated/runtime artifacts MUST NOT occupy governed source roots, and declared Fortress-controlled canonical paths MUST use exact spelling.
rationale: Project-declared placement reduces structural entropy while preserving ecosystem-required names and avoiding a universal cross-language folder tree.
failure_prevented: Undeclared implementation islands, structurally unowned files, generated or runtime state mixed into source authority, and non-canonical Fortress-controlled path spelling.
applicability: Every stabilized governed repository inventory whose architecture declares repository placement policy under the applicable archetype.
evaluation: The Fortress core compares canonical observed paths with declared allowed top-level roots, component and artifact ownership, source roots, prohibited artifact classes, and exact canonical paths.

finding.message: An observed path violates the project-declared repository placement policy.

remediation: Move the path into a declared top-level and owned structural root, declare a defensible project-specific placement, remove prohibited generated/runtime state from source, or restore the exact canonical Fortress-controlled path spelling.
valid_example: A Rust workspace keeps Cargo.toml as explicitly owned repository metadata while implementation resides under the project's declared crates/ root.
invalid_example: An undeclared tools/ implementation island appears, generated output is placed beneath a prohibited source root, or .Fortress/project.json replaces the declared .fortress/project.json path.
exception_policy: Ecosystem-required names are modeled explicitly and are not violations. Future exemptions must not silently redefine the project's declared structure.
history: Introduced during CHG-SNAPSHOT-0006 as a project-declared structural rule following the Fortress entropy doctrine.
